source_snapshot.procedure: Send in-band Sensor/Event 04h/02h with unspecified request data described as the seven EvMRev-through-Event-Data bytes used by IPMB messaging, after clearing logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Command should be sent without any error.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL proposes only `00 10 00`, an incomplete and unapproved example.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED pending an exact event vector, decoded SEL/routing outcome, side-effect containment and retention/cleanup policy.

old_problem: The historical review correctly prohibited an undefined event injection but assumed a seven-byte request and did not use the standard system-interface format. IPMI 2.0 section 29.3 requires an additional System Software Generator ID on KCS/SMIC/BT/SSIF, followed by EvMRev, sensor type/number, direction/type and one to three event-data bytes. Thus this IB case uses six to eight request bytes, while the related OOB/LAN variant retains the IPMB-style form. The concrete software-owned sensor vector and no-PEF-side-effect policy are finite Project inputs.
disposition_reason: Define a parameterized in-band Platform Event using Sensor/Event 04h/02h and the standard system-interface fields: encoded System Software ID, EvMRev 04h, valid sensor type, non-FFh software-owned sensor number, direction/event type, mandatory Event Data1 and optional Data2/Data3 only as the selected event class requires. Before injection, prove the vector is synthetic/authorized and matches no enabled PEF filter or downstream automation that can alert, power, reset, cycle or interrupt. Preserve SEL and receiver baselines, inject once, and correlate the exact decoded/raw resulting record and permitted downstream behavior. Retain the test record by default; never clear SEL, invent a hardware fault identity, use the OOB seven-byte form, repeat the event or claim completion alone is PASS.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1064-1066 and 1071, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests_gpt_merged, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The code is unique. Related OOB row 1192 / Wistron-BMC-00482-V002 / variant ecd1b8f4e778ab5d was directly read and remains separate. Formal queue sequence 69 was independently verified as row 1071 / variant bc33ada8ab4575b0.

IPMI v2.0 section 29.3/Table 29-4 defines Platform Event under Sensor/Event NetFn 04h, command 02h. IPMB-format transports, including LAN, carry seven data fields because requester address/LUN supplies Generator ID; system-side interfaces must carry Generator ID as request byte 1 and therefore have a different payload.

For a system interface, the request is Generator ID, EvMRev, Sensor Type, Sensor Number, Event Direction/Type, Event Data1 and optional Event Data2/Data3. The source's seven-field description omits Generator ID and belongs to its separate OOB/IPMB-formatted coverage.

Sections 5.4-5.5 require Generator ID bit0=1 for a System Software ID. An approved System Management Software ID is a 7-bit value 20h-2Fh encoded as the odd byte 41h-5Fh; the exact allocation must avoid impersonating BIOS, SMI, OEM or another producer.

EvMRev is 04h for the current format. Sensor type, sensor number, direction/type and event data must form one coherent standard or Project-defined software-owned sensor event. Sensor number FFh is reserved; an arbitrary real hardware sensor identity would create false evidence.

Section 29.7/Table 29-6 defines class-specific Event Data. Data1 is required; Data2/Data3 are optional only when their presence and selector bits agree. An omitted optional byte is transferred to SEL as FFh. DeepSeek's three bytes cannot satisfy even the minimum system-interface payload.

The BMC normally records the message in SEL and may also place it in the Event Message Buffer or process it through PEF. A syntactically valid event can therefore trigger alerts, power-down, reset, power-cycle, diagnostic interrupt or external automation; preflight must prove the allowlisted vector has no prohibited match.

Command completion is only acceptance. PASS needs a new correlated SEL/event record whose generator, revision, sensor, direction/type and data match exactly, plus an observation that only explicitly allowed PEF/alert behavior occurred. Baseline log deletion would destroy this oracle.

ED-03 supplies standard semantics; ED-15 prohibits an undefined oracle; ED-16 requires isolation/tool/recovery for injection; ED-17 preserves SEL before any deletion; ED-19 separates IB/OOB formats; ED-28/ED-30 contain recovery; ED-38 prohibits automatic retry.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Platform Event (IB 04h/02h) system-software identity, SEL correlation and PEF containment
test_case.purpose: Inject exactly one authorized synthetic event over the local system interface using the correct System Software Generator ID format, prove its exact SEL/receiver representation and absence of unapproved PEF/alert actions, and preserve the resulting audit evidence without impersonating hardware or substituting the OOB payload format.
required_package: Approved chassis/BMC/firmware and local KCS/SMIC/BT/SSIF path, current SEL/event-receiver/PEF/alert configuration, capacity check and independent management/recovery observation

Versioned event contract allocating one System Management Software ID (7-bit 20h-2Fh and encoded odd byte 41h-5Fh), a software-owned non-FFh sensor number, sensor type, event direction/type and class-valid data1/data2/data3 with exact decoded meaning

Preflight proof that the vector is synthetic and does not match any enabled PEF action, alert policy, webhook, ticket, remediation, shutdown/reset/power-cycle/diagnostic rule or uncontained external consumer

Versioned in-band raw runner accepting exactly six to eight validated bytes after 04h/02h, one-shot/no-retry enforcement, SEL raw/decoded correlation by record ID/time/fields and protected evidence storage
Immediate owner confirmation, maintenance/containment window, expected completion and SEL/receiver result, permitted downstream effect list, retention-by-default policy and recovery escalation
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED ONE-SHOT EVENT PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve SEL, Event Message Buffer, PEF/alert and downstream baselines; do not clear them. Validate that Generator ID decodes to the allocated System Management Software ID with bit0=1, EvMRev=04h, sensor number is not FFh, the software-owned sensor contract matches sensor type and event direction/type, and Event Data1-3 obey the selected threshold/discrete/OEM class including optional-byte selector rules. Prove from the active PEF/alert/downstream configuration that this exact vector cannot cause any unapproved action; otherwise remain NOT READY. Record the last SEL record ID and start all monitors. Display the complete six/eight-byte vector, decoded meaning and containment for immediate confirmation; send exactly once over `-I open` Sensor/Event 04h/02h [GEN_ID 04 SENSOR_TYPE SENSOR_NUM DIR_TYPE DATA1 (DATA2) (DATA3)]. Require completion 00h, then locate exactly the attributable new record without deleting history; compare raw and decoded generator/software ID, revision, sensor, direction/type and all data bytes, treating omitted Data2/Data3 as FFh in SEL. Correlate allowed receiver/PEF/alert observations and prove no prohibited external action occurred. Retain and label the synthetic record by default. Never use the source's seven-byte OOB layout, DeepSeek's partial bytes, a real-fault identity, an unreviewed OEM vector, log clear, automatic retry or a second injection after any mismatch.
test_case.expected_result: The single correctly formatted 04h/02h request returns completion 00h. Exactly one attributable logical synthetic event appears in the expected SEL/receiver path within the approved window; its System Software Generator ID, EvMRev 04h, sensor type/number, assertion/deassertion and event type, Data1 and present/FF-substituted optional data bytes equal the approved contract. SEL history and capacity remain intact, and only the explicitly permitted PEF/alert behavior occurs—no power, reset, diagnostic, false external alert or automated remediation. A malformed/missing Generator ID, unmatched or multiple logical records, decoded-field mismatch, full SEL, prohibited side effect or missing retained evidence is FAIL/NOT READY without retry.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact Source Key/variant, system-interface six-to-eight-byte format, valid allocated software ID/sensor/event semantics, documented no-prohibited-PEF match, one completion, exact new SEL/receiver field correlation, allowed-only downstream effects and preserved history. The source seven-byte IPMB/OOB layout, DeepSeek's three bytes, command success alone, arbitrary hardware sensor identity, reserved/invalid fields, uncontained alert/RAS behavior, cleared SEL, OOB evidence substituted for this IB identity, automatic retry or deletion without preserved evidence cannot pass. N/A requires authoritative proof that the platform cannot accept standard system-interface Platform Event messages.
safety_gate: Use only the local system interface and its Generator ID request byte. Row 1192 OOB/LAN uses a different message form and remains independent coverage.
Use an allocated software-owned identity and explicitly synthetic non-FFh sensor number; never claim a physical fault, temperature, voltage, memory or RAS condition that did not occur.

Inspect active PEF filters, alert policies and external automation against the exact vector before injection. Any possible power/reset/cycle/diagnostic/uncontained alert match makes the run NOT READY.

Preserve SEL and downstream baselines and verify capacity. Do not clear SEL before or after; retention is the default. Any optional record-specific cleanup requires separately preserved evidence and explicit owner authorization.
Inject exactly once only after immediate confirmation. Stop on nonzero completion, missing/extra/mismatched record, alert or platform side effect and preserve all evidence.

No automatic retry. If an unexpected PEF or external action occurs, do not send deassertion or another event blindly; isolate downstream automation through the approved recovery owner and retain the triggering record.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; chassis/BMC/firmware/system-interface identity; official IB-vs-OOB format authority; distinct row-1192 OOB Source Key/variant
Approved software ID allocation and encoded Generator ID, synthetic sensor/event contract, class-specific data validation and decoded expected SEL fields
Pre-injection SEL last-record/capacity, Event Receiver, PEF/filter/alert/downstream baseline and exact no-prohibited-match analysis
Versioned runner hash, immediate approval, redacted complete request, one completion and timestamp/record-ID correlation
Raw plus decoded new SEL/receiver record, optional-byte FF substitution, permitted downstream observations and proof of no prohibited action
Retention/any separately authorized record-specific cleanup evidence and engineer PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A verdict, with no DUT action by the review agent
test_case.recovery: No persistent configuration is intentionally changed; the generated SEL/event record is retained as audit evidence. On nonzero completion or record mismatch, stop without another injection and preserve every monitor. On an unexpected alert/PEF/platform action, the authorized owner follows the pre-approved isolation and service-recovery plan while the agent performs no reset, power action, counter-event or retry. Do not clear SEL. If policy later requires removing the synthetic artifact, first export immutable raw/decoded evidence and use only an explicitly approved record-specific method; if unavailable, retain the record rather than erase unrelated history.

source_conflict.reason: Official sections 29.3-29.7 resolve the IB payload and record oracle: the review layer adds the required System Software Generator ID, permits only class-valid optional data, rejects the OOB seven-byte and partial example forms, and replaces log clearing/success-only Criteria with exact retained evidence.

blocked.reason: Core system-interface format, Software ID encoding, event-field semantics and SEL mapping are standardized. Exact allocated synthetic vector and side-effect allowlist are bounded Project package/configuration inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Exact BMC/firmware/system interface; allocated software ID and synthetic sensor/event vector; active PEF/alert/downstream no-match analysis; SEL capacity/baseline; allowed effects, retention policy, maintenance confirmation and recovery owner.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER EVENT-INJECTION DEFINITION ONLY; NO PLATFORM EVENT, SEL MUTATION/CLEAR, PEF ACTION, ALERT, POWER, RESET OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7
external_authorities.application: Sections 5.4-5.5, 29.3-29.7 and Tables 5-4, 29-4 through 29-6 define the system-interface Generator ID byte, Software ID ranges, EvMRev 04h, sensor/event fields, class-specific optional data and SEL substitution; they distinguish this format from IPMB/LAN messages and describe SEL/Event Buffer/PEF processing.

project_authority: Platform/SEL/PEF owners allocate the synthetic System Software ID and sensor contract, verify the complete event vector against active filters and external consumers, approve the one-shot window/effects/retention and own recovery/verdicts. They cannot approve a physical-fault impersonation, the OOB seven-byte or partial payload, an event with possible uncontained action, log clearing, completion-only PASS, automatic retry or evidence deletion without preservation.
